Success metrics (targets & timeframes): 1) CSM weekly active usage in the Q2 pilot +25–35 percentage points within 3 months (target +15 p.p. product-wide at 6 months) to drive coverage→NRR; 2) pilot‑cohort gross churn down 20–30% relative within 6 months (e.g., 12%→~9–10%) contributing toward the 12→8% goal; 3) renewal forecast error (MAPE) reduced 15–25% within 3–6 months to improve renewal capture and expansions; 4) playbook adoption of 40–60% of at‑risk accounts in pilot within 3 months and pilot CS‑leader NPS ≥45.  
Experimentation & rollout (concrete): 6‑account Q2 pilot (3 mid‑market, 3 expansion) with feature flags; A/B tests for Task Feed ranking (control + 1 variant) and Forecast visualization (control + 1 variant); phased opt‑in rollout for Health Score Editor with 2 config‑complexity variants; cap at 2 concurrent experiments per account and max 3 variants total.

H2 contingency sequencing (prioritized): if Health Editor misses targets, pivot to managed templated score services and accelerate the targeted rules‑engine refactor; if Task Feed/CRM sync fails, deprioritize broader playbook library and instead invest in CRM‑embedded cards and tighter workflow integration; if Renewal dashboards underperform, shift H2 effort to automated playbook ROI measurement and executive one‑pagers to protect progress toward the 12‑month NRR, churn, CSM usage, and NPS goals.

rounds.consequence: Your concrete success metrics, lean experimentation design, and modest reallocation for instrumentation are accepted as the way you will evaluate and adapt the H1 plan in this planning cycle. Stakeholders see your stop/scale rules and H2 contingencies as a structured approach to managing risk while still aiming for the NRR, churn, CSM usage, and NPS goals.

The rules for context evolution, resource adjustments, and actor behavior are followed consistently across the eight rounds, with incremental, trend-consistent updates and realistic capacity tweaks.
